propositions: Rebar must safely delegate credential issuance, retrieval, persistence, refresh, rotation, and invalidation to upstream SDKs, helpers, CI systems, and deployments rather than implementing a universal secret broker.
Static credentials in long-running processes require restart or redeploy to observe changes; no automatic hot-reload cache or environment-variable polling is supported.

Deployment supplies operation-certificate secrets via exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (file) or multiline REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY (environment) before process startup; Rebar validates and materializes into a process-owned 0700-directory 0600-file without runtime SSM/boto3 coupling.

Provider-native credential and identity capabilities are injected into Rebar-owned SDK factories; operation snapshots structurally exclude SecretStr/SecretBytes carriers; static values are unwrapped only inside provider-specific adapters.

Subprocess children inherit ambient environment for native Git/SSH/AWS credential-process chains; Rebar overlays materialized static values only for owning children and removes exact declared secret names from unrelated siblings without global os.environ mutation.

All 17 application-sensitive inputs are classified as provider-owned, deployment-owned static adapter inputs, or Rebar-owned security material; no runtime keyring adapter, file watcher, or cloud-secret retrieval layer is added in initial scope.
